II.—For the purposes of this section, the competence of a Court shall be determined irrespective 
of any provisions as to a right of appeal from the decision of such Court. 


Explanation II.—The matter above referred to must in the former suit have been alleged by one 
party and either denied or admitted, expressly or impliedly, by the other. Explanation 


IV.—Any matter which might and ought to have been made ground of defence or attack in such 
former suit shall be deemed to have been a matter directly and substantially in issue in such suit. 


Explanation V.—Any relief claimed in the plaint, which is not expressly granted by the decree, 
shall for the purposes of this section, be deemed to have been refused. 


Explanation VI.—Where persons litigate bona fide in respect of a public right or of a private 
right claimed in common for themselves and others, all persons interested in such right shall, for the 
purposes of this section, be deemed to claim under the persons so litigating . / 


Explanation VII.—The provisions of this section shall apply to a proceeding for the execution of 
a decree and references in this section to any suit, issue or former suit shall be construed as references, 
respectively, to a proceeding for the execution of the decree, question arising in such proceeding and a 
former proceeding for the execution of that decree. 


Explanation VIII. —An issue heard and finally decided by a Court of limited jurisdiction, 
competent to decide such issue, shall operate as res judicata in a subsequent suit, notwithstanding that 
such Court of limited jurisdiction was not competent to try such subsequent suit or the suit in which such 
issue has been subsequently raised 


Since, the facts in issue are not substantially the same, then the case in hand and the referred cases, 
it is held that the claim of the Workman is not barred by res judicata. 


Issue No. 4 is answered accordingly. 
Issue No. 2 - 


The relevant portion of the Railway Board Circular dated 24/25.0.985 is being reproduced as 
follows: 


“Reliving at intermediate stations — 


Whenever possible, the break in duty may be considered at en-route stations having 
resting facilities, after ॥0 to ॥2 hours duty with a fresh state of staff taking over and where this is not 
feasible, the staff should be given adequate compensatory rest at home station to keep this cumulative duty 
hours below permissible limit of /04 hours for 74 days period. 


It also comes out from perusal of this letter that it is with respect to the deployment of AC and 
Electrical staff in the Air condition and power coaches of various trains including Rajdhani, Deluxe and 
other trains. 


This is also not disputed that as per circulars, the duty hours for AC Mechanics/Helpers in the 
Maintenance Hours is 96 hours for 4 days and they will be entitled to overtime allowance as per relevant 
provisions when they work above the ceiling limit. The letter dated 4.05.205 issued by the Assistant 
Personnel Officer, wherein he states that the AC Technical Staff of Durg (AC Technicians/Helpers working 
in the Maintenance Roster) should be 04 hours as instead of 96 hours as per Circular of Railway Board 
dated 24/25.0.985. The relevant portion of this circular has been mentioned earlier, this circular talks only 
with respect to the AC staff in escorting duty and not in maintenance duty. Hence, this letter and this 
interpretation of the Assistant Personnel Officer of the Railways in the Office of South Eastern Railways at 
Raipur made by him in his letter No. E/PS/R/Welfare/TA&OT/0I/204 dated 4.05.205 is nothing but 
misinterpretation of the Railway Board Circular of 24/25.0.985. 


It is relevant to mention on this juncture the fact that, from the RTI document filed from the side of 
Workman Union, the AC Mechanics and Helpers working in the Maintenance Roster in West Central

also the action of Management is discriminatory and arbitrary. 


Hence on the basis of above discussion, the action of Management on the basis of this letter in 
not granting overtime to the AC Mechanic/Helpers working within the Maintenance Roster who have 
worked beyond the ceiling limit of 96 Hours in 4 days is held unjustified in law. 


Issue No. 2 is answered accordingly. 


On the basis of above discussion the reference is answered as follows- 


4426 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 6, 2026/VAISAKHA 26, 948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 
AWARD 


The action of Management of South Easter Central Railway through its Senior Divisional

As per letter dated ३30/000/2023 by the Government of India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi, the reference 
has been made to this Tribunal under Section-l0 of Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (in short the ‘Act’) as per 
Notification No. RP-8(4-06)/2023-ES.III dt. 30/07/2023. The dispute under reference relates to: 


“Whether the action on the part of the management of South Eastern Central Railway Bilaspur (CG) in 
retrenching the workman Shri Yashwant Giri Goswami, S/o Laxmi Giri Goswami, substitute Telephone Attendant 
cum Dak Khalasi, on the basis of purported resignation letter is legal and justified? If not, to what relief, the

The case of the workman is mainly that he was appointed by the Senior Administrative Officer on the post 
of Telephone Attendant-cum-Daak Khalasi in pay matrix level-I, 7" CPC vide order dated 22.04.209 and worked 
continuously till 30.06.202l without any break, his services were terminated by the department under an oral order 
without notice or compensation. He had acquired permanent status of an employee, this action of termination of his 
service by the department is in violation of section 25-F and 25-G of the Act hence, is unjust, illegal and arbitrary. He 
has requested that set aside his termination, he be reinstated with back-wages and benefits. 


The department has taken a case that, the workman was appointed vide letter dated 22.04.209. He 
accepted the terms and conditions of the offer letter and thereafter, Office Order dated 29.04.20l9 was issued, 
appointing him as substitute Telephone Attendant-cum-Daak Khalasi in pay matrix level-I, 77 CPC. He was attached 
with Deputy Chief Engineer and joined under him under para 4 of the Establishment Rule No. 250/200 as Telephone 
Attendant-cum-Daak Khalasi.After joining on 29.04.209, the workman submitted a letter dated 02.05.209 to the 
department stating that he was not willing to work and his services be terminated, this letter was forwarded by Deputy

Chief Engineer (General) to Senior Personnel Officer, Headquarter vide his letter dated 06.05.20I9 and after the 
approval of Principal Chief Engineer his services were terminated from 02.05.20l9 vide Office Order dated 
07.06.209. Thus according to management, he submitted his resignation just after four days in service which was 
duly accepted. Hence, according to department, the workman was never disengaged by them rather he himself 
resigned from service. Department has requested that the reference be answered against the workman. 


In his rejoinder, the workman has denied the case of the department that he himself resigned. 


In Evidence, the workman filed his affidavit as his Examination-in-chief, he was cross-examined by the 
department. The department filed affidavit of its witness Snehasish Ghosh as his Examination-in-chief. The 
department filed and proved documents Ex-M/I to M/I0, to be referred to as and when require. 


I have heard argument of Learned Counsel for Workman Mr. Shailesh Mishra and Mr. S.K. Gupta, Learned 
Counsel for Department. The workman side has filed written submission, also which are part of record. I have gone 
through the written submission and record as well. 


On perusal of record in light of rival arguments, the sole issue which arises for determination is. 


Whether the services of the workman stood terminated on the basis of his resignation letter dated 
02.05.209 and order passed by the Officers of Department on this letter accepting his resignation? 


In his statement, the workman has denied that he filed any resignation letter. He denied his signature on the 
resignation letter. The management witness has proved this resignation letter. In these circumstances, the burden was 
on the workman to prove by evidence of forgery that his signatures on his resignation dated 02.05.209 are in fact not 
done by him. He has not discharged his burden. Hence, the fact that he filed his resignation letter as stated above is 
held proved. 


Learned Counsel for the workman has also submitted that, even if the workman had filed his resignation 
letter but, termination of his services could not be held complete till its acceptance of resignation letter and order with 
respect to dismissal of service was communicated to him. He has referred to Judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court in 
the case of, State of Punjab vs Amar Singh Harika, 7966 SCC Online SC 48, in the case referred, the employee was 
found guilty of misconduct in a departmental enquiry, he was sent a communication by the department to the effect 
that in light of finding of enquiry holding him guilty, he could exercise his option to resign. Pursuant to that letter the 
employee sent his resignation. Order of dismissal was passed on the resignation. The question which was before the 
Hon’ble Supreme Court was whether the order of dismissal on the basis of his resignation letter would be effective 
from the date of communication or from the date of order. The Five Judges Bench of Hon’ble Supreme Court held 
that, it would be effective from the date of its communication or its publication. 


Learned Counsel for workman has submitted that since, this order was never communicated to him or 
published, it could not be held effective. Office memorandum dated 07.06.20l9 which declares that service of the 
workman shall stand terminated from the date of his resignation letter dated 02.05.209 and a copy was ordered to be 
sent to the workman along with other offices including Pay and Accounts Office, in such circumstances, it cannot be 
said that the order was not published, may be, it may not served on him. 


Even otherwise, though the case of the workman was that he worked till 202, but he could not produce any 
evidence to support his this claim that he worked for 240 days in any year, but he could at least produce his pay slips 
or attendance slips to corroborate his this case, in absence of such evidence, his case that he worked for 240 days in a 
year also held not proved. 


“In light of above discussion, holding the termination of services of the workman by Department, just and 
legal, the workman is held entitled to no relief.” 


The reference stands answered accordingly. 
No order as to cost.

As per letter dated 24/05/207 by the Government of India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi, the reference is 
made to this Tribunal under Section-l0 of Industrial Disputes Act, |947 (in short the ‘Act’)as per Notification 
No. L-20/30/206 (IR(B-D) dt. 24/05/207. The dispute under reference relates to: 


"Whether the demand of Union claiming difference of wages in favour of Sh. Radheshyam Rathore daily 
wage employee from 6.05.83 to 05.07.44 is justified or not? If so, what relief the daily wager is entitled 
for?" 


Case of the Workman Union is that, the Workman Radheyshyam Rathore was appointed as a peon on 
temporary basis by the then State Bank of Indore in its Sarangpur Branch on scale wage Rs. 245 with DA from the 
period 6.05.983 to 23.05.983 and 07..983 to 2..983. Thereafter he was appointed as daily wager on 
8.08.986 on a daily wage under oral orders of the Branch Manager and worked till 05.0.20l! when he was 
terminated without any notice or compensation for which he has filed another case. His claim in the case in hand is 
that he is entitled to the wages paid to the temporary staff of the Bank discharging the same duties of the Peon but he 
was paid only wages on Collector Rate, which is unjust and illegal, the Union has prayed that the Workman be paid 
its all wages accordingly. 


Case of the Management is that the Workman was appointed for total period of about 2 weeks, on a leave 
vacancy for which he was paid scale wages. Thereafter, he worked as a daily wager for which he was paid wages on 
Collector Rates. It is further the case of the Management that the scale wages according to bi partite settlement are 
admissible to the Regularly Appointed staff and not to the daily wager. 


Both the parties have filed their affidavits. They have cross-examined by their adversaries. They have filed 
some certain documents which were referred to as and when require. 


I have heard argument of Learned Counsel Mr. Arun Patel for the Workman and Mr. Pranay Choubey for 
the Management Bank and have gone through the record. 


The reference itself is the issue for determination in the case in hand. 


[भाग aves 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 6, 2026/वैशाख 26, 948 4433 


The main question involve for consideration is whether the bi-partite settlement applies to the daily wager 
also or not. The workman side could not cite any provisions in the bi partite settlement in this respect. It also comes 
out from perusal of the bi partite settlement that, it is applicable to the staff who are on regular appointment may be as 
a permanent or a temporary workers. Hence, the claim of the Workman with respect to the period in which he has 
worked as a daily wager with the Bank is not admissible in law with regard to parity to the wages paid to the regular 
employees. 


With regard to period he was appointed on temporary basis on leave vacancy, was for two times as 
mentioned in his statement of claim. The workman side itself admits that he was paid scale wage for this period. 


In the light of above discussion and evidence the reference is answered as follows. 
AWARD 


Holding the demand of Union claiming difference of wages in favour of Sh. Radheshyam Rathore daily 
wage employee from 76.05.63 to 05.07.474 is unjustified and against law. The Workman is entitled to no relief. 


No order as to cost.

Election Expenses; and

O.N. 10.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of Haryana, 2024 for 2-Kurukshetra 
Parliamentary Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. O.N. 114(E), 
dated 29" April, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election for 2-Kurukshetra Parliamentary Constituency of 
Haryana, 2024 was declared by the Returning Officer on 47 June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the 
account of Election Expenses was 47 July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the DEO, Kurukshetra’s report dated 30.07.2024 forwarded by the Chief Electoral 
Officer, Haryana vide his letter No. 6/Elect-Exp./ GEL-2024/2AE-7497 dated 05.08.2024, under sub-rule (1) of Rule 
89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Er. Vishal Kumar a contesting candidate from 2-Kurukshetra 
Parliamentary Constituency has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Kurukshetra a Show-Cause 
notice No. 76/HR-LS/2/2024/CEMS-I, dated 201 January, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Er. Vishal Kumar for not lodging of 
account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Er. Vishal Kumar was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Kurukshetra District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Kurukshetra vide his letter no. Election-2025/173 dated 
20.02.2025 has informed that the notice was duly served and received by Er. Vishal Kumar’s Mother ( name Smt. 
Prem Kumari), on dated 18.01.2025; and 


28 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 16, 2026/V AISAKHA 26, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(iii)] 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Kurukshetra in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. 
Election-2025/297 dated 09.04.2025 has reported that Er. Vishal Kumar has not submitted account of election 
expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Er. Vishal Kumar has neither furnished any reason nor explanation 
to the Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; 
and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Er. Vishal Kumar 
has failed to lodge account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Er. Vishal Kumar, House No. 11, Moti Bagh, Gobindpura, 
Yamuna Nagar, Haryana-135001, a contesting candidate for 2-Kurukshetra Parliamentary Constituency of 
Haryana in General Election to Lok Sabha, 2024 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of 
either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory 
for a period of three years from the date of this order.

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 9th March, 2026 


O.N. 12.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of Punjab, 2024, for 03- Khadoor Sahib 
Parliamentary Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification 
No. 464/EPS/2024(7), dated 7 May, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 03- Khadoor Sahib Parliamentary Constituency of Punjab, 2024 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 04" June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 4" July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 04.07.2024 of DEO, Tarn Taran under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2024/R-7458, dated 
22.07.2024 stating that Sh. Sarabjit Singh, a contesting candidate from 03- Khadoor Sahib Parliamentary 
Constituency of state of Punjab has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 76/PB- 
LS/3/2024/CEMS-I, dated 317 January, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections 
Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Sarabjit Singh, for not lodging of the account of Election 
Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Sarabjit Singh was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his election expenses with the 
District Election Officer, Tarn Taran District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the DEO, Tarn Taran has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Smt. 
Jasbir Kaur (Mother of Sh. Sarabjit Singh) on 21.11.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Tarn Taran in his Supplementary Report, received through the 
CEO, Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2026/R-1265, dated 17.02.2026 has reported that Sh. Sarabjit Singh has not 
submitted any representation or statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. 
Sarabjit Singh has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India for failure to 
lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“Tf the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(iii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 16, 2026/वैशाख 26, 1948 33 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.’’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Sarabjit Singh 
has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; 
and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Sarabjit Singh, resident of Ward No. 8, Gaushala Road, Near 
Kaushal Farm, Zira and a contesting candidate from 03- Khadoor Sahib Parliamentary Constituency of State of 
Punjab, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the 
Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date 
of this order.

New Delhi, the 17th November, 2025 


O.N. 15.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of Assam, 2024, for 02- Dhubri Parliamentary 
Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/EPS/2024(3), dated 
12" April, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 02- Dhubri Parliamentary Constituency of Assam, 2024 was 
declared by the Returning Officer on 047 June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 4" July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 16.08.2024 of DEO, Dhubri under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the Conduct 
of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Assam vide his letter no. ELE.64/2023/496, dated 21.08.2024 
stating that Sh. Alakesh Roy, a contesting candidate from 02- Dhubri Parliamentary Constituency of state of Assam 
has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ 
No. 76/AS-LS/02/2024/CEMS-I, dated 307 December, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct 
of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Alakesh Roy, for not lodging of the account of 
Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Alakesh Roy was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his election expenses with the 
District Election Officer, Dhubri District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and

WHEREAS, the DEO, Dhubri has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Sh. Alakesh 
Roy on 10.01.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Dhubri in his Supplementary Report, received through the CEO, 
Assam vide his letter no. ELE.64/2023/Vol-I/19, dated 20.09.2025 has reported that Sh. Alakesh Roy has not 
submitted any representation or statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. 
Alakesh Roy has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India for failure to 
lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.’’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Alakesh Roy has 
failed to lodge the account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Alakesh Roy, resident of Vill- Uttar Raipur Pt.II, P.O. 
Moterjhar, P.S. Golakganj, Dist. Dhubri, Assam, Pin-783334 and a contesting candidate from 02- Dhubri 
Parliamentary Constituency of state of Assam, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either 
House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a 
period of three years from the date of this order.

election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her

stating that Ms. Radharani Biswas, a contesting candidate from 02- Dhubri Parliamentary Constituency of state of 
Assam has failed to lodge the account of her election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 
76/AS-LS/02/2024/CEMS-I, dated 307 December, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Ms. Radharani Biswas, for not lodging of the account 
of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Ms. Radharani Biswas was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of her election expenses with the 
District Election Officer, Dhubri District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the DEO, Dhubri has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Ms. Radharani 
Biswas on 13.01.2025; and

Assam vide his letter no. ELE.64/2023/Vol-I/19, dated 20.09.2025 has reported that Ms. Radharani Biswas has not

(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this

O.N. 18.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of Punjab, 2024, for 06- Anandpur Sahib 
Parliamentary Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification 
No. 464/EPS/2024(7), dated 7 May, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 06- Anandpur Sahib Parliamentary Constituency of Punjab, 2024 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 04" June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 4" July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 05.07.2024 of DEO, Rupnagar under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2024/R-7458, dated 
22.07.2024 stating that Ms. Kiran Jain, a contesting candidate from 06-Anandpur Sahib Parliamentary 
Constituency of state of Punjab has failed to lodge the account of her election expenses, as required under law; and

LS/06/2024/CEMS-I, dated 31“ January, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections 
Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Ms. Kiran Jain, for not lodging of the account of Election

election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election for 10-Faridabad Parliamentary Constituency of 
Haryana, 2024 was declared by the Returning Officer on 47 June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the

No. 76/HR-LS/10/2024/CEMS-I, dated 20" December, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the

Gokak Assembly Constituency in General Election to Legislative Assembly of Karnataka, 2023 has failed to lodge

76/KT-LA/02/2023/CEMS-II, dated 18" August, 2023 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Jagadeesh C. K., for not lodging of the account of 
Election Expenses; and

Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Jagadeesh C. K. was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission

‘Show Cause Notice’ and notice was also pasted on the wall of the residence and a Panchanama was prepared on 
23.08.2023; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Belagavi in his Supplementary Report dated 22.09.2023 and

O.N. 27.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of Haryana, 2024 for 80-Ferozepur

WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election for 80-Ferozepur Jhirka Assembly Constituency of 
Haryana, was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" October, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account 
of Election Expenses was 77 November, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the DEO, Nuh’s report forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, Haryana vide his letter 
no. 6/Elect-Exp./GELA-HR-2024/Elec-2025/2AE-692 dated 05.02.2025, under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Mohammad Hashim a contesting candidate from 80-Ferozepur Jhirka 
Assembly Constituency has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Nuh a Show-Cause notice No. 
76/HR-LA/Exp. Account/2024/CEMS-I, dated 30™ April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Mohammad Hashim for not lodging 
of his account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Mohammad Hashim was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Nuh within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Nuh vide his letter no. Elec-2025/744 dated 10.06.2025 has 
informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Mohammad Hashim on 20.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Nuh in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. Elec-2025/744 
dated 10.06.2025 has reported that Sh. Mohammad Hashim has not submitted account of election expenses. Further, 
after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Mohammad Hashim has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the 
Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


70 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 16, 2026/V AISAKHA 26, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(iii)] 
WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years 
from the date of the order.”’;

do so; and

Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Mohammad Hashim, Village Mohammad Nagar, Tehsil 
Ferozepur Jhirka, District Nuh, Haryana, a contesting candidate for 80-Ferozepur Jhirka Assembly

State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

अपने निर्वाचन व्यय के लेखे दाखिल करने में असफल रहे हैं और उनके पास ऐसा करने में असफल रहने के लिए कोई भी 
उचित कारण अथवा औचित्य नहीं है, और

एतद्वारा घोषणा करता है कि विधान सभा के साधारण निर्वाचन, 2023 में राजस्थान राज्य के 80-राजाखेड़ा विधान सभा

राजस्थान, इस आदेश की तारीख से तीन वर्ष की अवधि के लिए संसद के किसी भी सदन अथवा राज्य अथवा संघ राज्य

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 27th November, 2025 


O.N. 30.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of Haryana, 2024 for 73-Kosli 
Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/ECI/HAR- 
LA/2024, dated 5h September, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana, 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" October, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 77 November, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by DEO, Rewari forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, 
Haryana vide his letter no. 6/Elect-Exp./GELA-HR-2024/Elec-2025/2AE-692 dated 05.02.2025, under sub-rule (1) of 
Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Naval Singh a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly 
Constituency has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Rewari a Show-Cause notice 
No. 76/HR-LA/Exp. Account/2024/CEMS-I, dated 30" April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Naval Singh for not lodging of his 
account of Election Expenses; and

WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Naval Singh was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Rewari within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari vide his letter no. Elec-2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has 
informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Naval Singh on 20.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. Elec- 
2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has reported that Sh. Naval Singh has not submitted account of election expenses. 
Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Naval Singh has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the 
Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years 
from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Naval Singh 
has failed to lodge account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Naval Singh, House No. 89, Village Mandiya Khurd, Tehsil 
and District Rewari, Haryana, a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana in 
General Election to Legislative Assembly, 2024 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of 
either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory 
for a period of three years from the date of this order.

LA/2024, dated 50 September, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her

WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana,

of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Mukesh Kumar a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly 
Constituency has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Rewari a Show-Cause notice No. 
76/HR-LA/Exp. Account/2024/CEMS-I, dated 30™ April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Mukesh Kumar for not lodging of his 
account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Mukesh Kumar was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Rewari within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari vide his letter no. Elec-2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has 
informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Mukesh Kumar on 20.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. Elec- 
2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has reported that Sh. Mukesh Kumar has not submitted account of election expenses. 
Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Mukesh Kumar has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the 
Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years

O.N. 33.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of Haryana, 2024 for 85-Prithla 
Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/ECI/HAR- 
LA/2024, dated 50 September, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and

WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election for 85-Prithla Assembly Constituency of Haryana, 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" October, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 77 November, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the DEO, Faridabad’s report forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, Haryana vide his 
letter no. 6/Elect-Exp./GELA-HR-2024/Elec-2025/2AE-692 dated 05.02.2025, under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Mukesh a contesting candidate from 85-Prithla Assembly Constituency has 
failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Faridabad a Show-Cause notice 
No. 76/HR-LA/Exp. Account/2024/CEMS-I, dated 30" April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Mukesh for not lodging of his 
account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Mukesh was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission explaining 
the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District Election 
Officer, Faridabad within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Faridabad vide his letter no. Elec-2025/1146 dated 10.06.2025 has 
informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Mukesh’s Nephew (name Piyush Kumar) on 
17.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Faridabad in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. Elec- 
2025/1146 dated 10.06.2025 has reported that Sh. Mukesh has not submitted account of election expenses. Further, 
after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Mukesh has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election 
Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 


“Tf the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 
(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 


Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years 
from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Mukesh has 
failed to lodge account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Mukesh, House No. 1472, Samaypur Road, Rajeev Colony, 
Ballabgarh, District-Faridabad, Haryana-121004, a contesting candidate for 85-Prithla Assembly Constituency 
of Haryana in General Election to Legislative Assembly, 2024 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a 
member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union 
Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Sandeep Kotra Advocate a contesting candidate from 16- 
Kalayat Assembly Constituency of state of Haryana has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required 
under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Kaithal a Show-Cause notice No. 
76/HR-LA/Exp. Account/2024/CEMS-I, dated 307 April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Sandeep Kotra Advocate for not 
lodging of his account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Sandeep Kotra Advocate was directed to submit representation in writing to the 
Commission explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with 
the District Election Officer, Kaithal District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Kaithal vide his letter no. Elec-2025/190 dated 10.06.2025 has

2025/190 dated 10.06.2025 has reported that Sh. Sandeep Kotra Advocate has not submitted account of election 
expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Sandeep Kotra Advocate has neither furnished any reason nor 
explanation to the Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as 
prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years

Kaithal, Haryana, a contesting candidate for 16-Kalayat Assembly Constituency of Haryana in General Election

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 7th May, 2025 


O.N. 36.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of West Bengal, 2024 for 08-Maldaha Dakshin 
Parliamentary Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 
464/EPS/2024(3) dated 12nd April, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer, an account of his election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent 
under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned elections for 08-Maldaha Dakshin Parliamentary 
Constituency of West Bengal, was declared by the Returning Officer on 47 June, 2024 and hence the last date for 
lodging the account of Election Expenses was 47 July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by the District Election Officer, Malda report dated 05.07.2024 
forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal vide his letter no. 4552-Home (Elec.) dated 197 July, 2024, 
under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan, a contesting 
candidate from 08-Maldaha Dakshin Parliamentary Constituency of state of West Bengal, has failed to lodge 
account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said reports of the District Election Officer, Malda a Show-Cause notice No. 
76/WB/PC-08/2024/CEMS-IV dated 177 September, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct 
of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan, for not lodging of his 
account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan, was directed to submit his representation in writing to the 
Commission explaining the reason for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the 
District Election Officer, Malda within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Malda vide his letter No. 945/VIII-9/Elec dated 24" December, 
2024 it has informed that the notice was served to Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan on 297 November, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Malda in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. 945/VIII- 
9/Elec dated 247 December, 2024 has reported that Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan has not submitted account of 
election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan has neither furnished any 
reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account as prescribed under law; 
and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three 
years from the date of the order.” 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Ahmed Hedatul 
Hasan, has failed to lodge his account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to 
do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Ahmed Hedatul Hasan resident of Vill- Hoglabari, P.O. - 
Kankuria, Dist - Murshidabad, West Bengal, Pin - 742202, a contesting candidate in 08-Maldaha Dakshin 
Parliamentary Constituency of General Election to the Lok Sabha of West Bengal, 2024 to be disqualified for 
being chosen as and for being a member of either House of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or Legislative 
Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order. 


[F. No. 76/WB/PC-08/2024/CEMS-IV] 
By Order,

New Delhi, the 9th September, 2025 


O.N. 39.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly, 2021 for 93-Pala Assembly 
Constituency of Kerala was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/KL- 
LA/2021, dated 197 March, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, as per the Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate 
at an election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent 
under Section 77 of the said act; and 

WHEREAS, the result of the election for 93-Pala Assembly Constituency was declared by the Returning 
Officer on 02" May, 2021 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election Expenses was 01“ June, 2021; 
and 


WHEREAS, the Commission having regard to the then prevailing pandemic situation of Covid-19, decided to 
condone any incidence of late submission of the account by candidate till 317 July, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report of the District Election Officer, Kottayam, under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, received through the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala vide his letter no. EL1/2/2021- 
ELEC; dated 02.11.2022 stating that Sh. Albin Mathew, a contesting candidate from 93-Pala Assembly 
Constituency of Kerala in General Election to the Legislative Assembly, 2021 has failed to lodge his account of 
election expenses, as required under law; and 

WHEREAS, on basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Kottayam a ‘Show Cause Notice’ No. 
76/KL-LA/93/2021/CEMS-II, dated 09" February, 2023 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Albin Mathew, for not lodging the account of 
Election Expenses; and

Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Albin Mathew was directed to submit a representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Kottayam within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala in his reports vide no. EL1/2/2021-ELEC; dated 03.11.2023

of the candidate, has reported that Sh. Albin Mathew has not submitted any representation or statement of correct 
account of election expenses. Besides, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Albin Mathew has neither furnished any 
reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election 
expenditure as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Albin Mathew 
has failed to lodge his account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of the Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the

for a period of three years from the date of this order.

New Delhi, the 12th August, 2025 


O.N. 42.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly, 2021 for 100-Kanjirappally 
Assembly Constituency of Kerala was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification 
No. 464/KL-LA/2021, dated 127 March, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, as per the Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate 
at an election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent 
under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 100-Kanjirappally Assembly Constituency was declared by the 
Returning Officer on 021 May, 2021 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election Expenses was 
017 June, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, the Commission having regard to the then prevailing pandemic situation of Covid-19, decided to 
condone any incidence of late submission of the account by candidate till 317 July, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report of the District Election Officer, Kottayam, under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, received through the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala vide his letter no. EL1/2/2021- 
ELEC; dated 24.08.2021 stating that Sh. Ashik M. M., a contesting candidate from 100-Kanjirapally Assembly 
Constituency of Kerala in General Election to the Legislative Assembly, 2021 has failed to lodge his account of 
election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Kottayam a ‘Show Cause Notice’ No. 
76/KL-LA/2021/CEMS-II, dated 06" October, 2021 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Ashik M. M., for not lodging the account of 
Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 


Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Ashik M. M. was directed to submit a representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and 


also to lodge account of election expenses with the District Election Officer, Kottayam within 20 days from the date 
of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala, vide his report no. EL1/2/2021-ELEC dated 30.07.2025, has 
forwarded to the Commission the original certified copy of the notice, which was served to the aforesaid candidate, as 
certified by the District Election Officer, Kottayam; 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Kottayam in his Supplementary Report dated 29.07.2025 as 
forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala vide his letter no. EL1/2/2021-ELEC; dated 30.07.2025 on account 
of the candidate, has reported that Sh. Ashik M. M. has not submitted any representation or statement of correct 
account of election expenses. Besides, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Ashik M. M. has neither furnished any 
reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election 
expenditure as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.’’;

failed to lodge his account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of the Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Ashik M. M., resident of - Mangalathu Anickadu P.O. and a 
contesting candidate from 100-Kanjirappally Assembly Constituency of Kerala in General Election to the 
Legislative Assembly, 2021, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the 
Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three 
years from the date of this order.

O.N. 43.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly, 2021 for 97-Kottayam Assembly 
Constituency of Kerala was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/KL- 
LA/2021, dated 12 March, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, as per the Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate 
at an election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent 
under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 97-Kottayam Assembly Constituency was declared by the 
Returning Officer on 027 May, 2021 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election Expenses was 01“ 
June, 2021; and 


WHEREAS, the Commission having regard to the then prevailing pandemic situation of Covid-19, decided to 
condone any incidence of late submission of the account by candidate till 317 July, 2021; and

WHEREAS, as per the report dated 30.09.2022 of the District Election Officer, Kottayam, under sub-rule (1) 
of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, received through the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala vide his 
letter no. EL1/2/2021-ELEC; dated 02.11.2022 stating that Sh. Arun Mangattu, a contesting candidate from 97- 
Kottayam Assembly Constituency of Kerala in General Election to the Legislative Assembly, 2021 has failed to 
lodge his account of election expenses in the manner as required under law; and 

WHEREAS, on basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Kottayam a ‘Show Cause Notice’ No. 
76/KL-LA/2021/CEMS-II, dated 157 February, 2023 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Arun Mangattu., for not lodging the account of 
Election Expenses in the manner; and 

WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Arun Mangattu was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account in the manner and also to submit the requisite vouchers of election 
expenses with the District Election Officer, Kottayam within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 

WHEREAS, the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala, vide its letter no. EL1/2/2021-ELEC; dated 03.11.2023, has 
forwarded the original acknowledgement of the ‘Show Cause Notice’ served to Sh. Arun Mangattu on 09.03.2023; 
and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Kottayam in his Supplementary Report dated 29.07.2025 as 
forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala vide his letter no. EL1/2/2021-ELEC; dated 30.07.2025 on account 
of the candidate, has reported that Sh. Arun Mangattu has not submitted any representation or requisite vouchers in 
respect of election expenses. Besides, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Arun Mangattu has neither furnished any 
reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of election expenditure in 
the manner as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 


, 


person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Arun Mangattu 
has failed to lodge his account of election expenses in the manner and has no good reason or justification for the 
failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of the Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Arun Mangattu resident of — Mangattu, Veloor P.O, Kottayam 
and a contesting candidate from 97-Kottayam Assembly Constituency of Kerala in General Election to the 
Legislative Assembly, 2021, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the 
Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three 
years from the date of this order.

O.N. 45.—WHEREAS, the Bye-election to 10-Dehra Assembly Constituency of Himachal Pradesh, 2024, 
was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 100/HP-LA/7/2024, dated 14" June, 
2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the Bye-election for 10-Dehra Assembly Constituency of Himachal Pradesh, 2024 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 137 July, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 12" August, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 12.08.2024 of DEO, Kangra under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Himachal Pradesh vide his letter no. 3-1/2024-ELN- 
EEM-IX-8462, dated 21.09.2024 stating that Ms. Sulekha Choudhary, a contesting candidate from Bye-election for 
10-Dehra Assembly Constituency of state of Himachal Pradesh has failed to lodge the account of her election 
expenses in the manner required as she failed to submit vouchers of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 
76/HP-LA/10/2024/CEMS-I(Bye), dated 12" November, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Ms. Sulekha Choudhary, for not lodging 
of the account of Election Expenses in the manner required; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Ms. Sulekha Choudhary was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission

explaining the reasons for not lodging the account in the manner required and also to lodge the vouchers of her 
election expenses with the District Election Officer, Kangra District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the 
notice; and 


WHEREAS, the DEO, Kangra has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Ms. Sulekha 
Choudhary on 05.03.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Kangra in his Supplementary Report no. 3-D/S (ELN)-3/2025-203; 
dated 19.01.2026 has reported that Ms. Sulekha Choudhary has not submitted the account of her election expenses 
in the manner required as she failed to submit vouchers of election expenses, as required under law. Further, after 
receipt of the said notice, Ms. Sulekha Choudhary has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election 
Commission of India for failure to lodge the account of her election expenses in the manner as prescribed under law; 
and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“Tf the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.’’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Ms. Sulekha 
Choudhary has failed to lodge the account of her election expenses in the manner required and has no good reason or 
justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Ms. Sulekha Choudhary, resident of Village and Post Office 
Kariara, Tehsil Dehra, District Kangra, Himachal Pradesh and a contesting candidate from Bye-election for 10- 
Dehra Assembly Constituency of State of Himachal Pradesh, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a 
member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union 
Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

O.N. 49.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of National Capital Territory of Delhi, 
2025 for 40-New Delhi Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification 
No. 464/ECI/DL-LA/2025, dated 10" January, 2025; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election Officer 
an account of his election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent under 
Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 40-New Delhi Assembly Constituency of National Capital Territory of 
Delhi, 2025 was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" February, 2025 and hence the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 10" March, 2025; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 11.03.2025 of DEO, New Delhi under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the Conduct 
of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi vide his letter No. 
CEO/COE/102(121)/2024/1637 dated 26.03.2025, Sh. Haidar Ali, a contesting candidate from 40-New Delhi Assembly 
Constituency of National Capital Territory of Delhi, 2025 has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required 
under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 76/दिल्ली 


वि0स0/व्यय लेखा/2025/सी0ई0एम0एस0-1, dated 29" April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct 


of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Haidar Ali, for not lodging of account of Election 
Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Haidar Ali, was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission explaining 
the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of election expenses with the District Election 
Officer, New Delhi, District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi, has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to 
Sh. Haidar Ali, on dated 07.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, New Delhi in his Supplementary Report dated 16.07.2025 has 
reported that Sh. Haidar Ali, has not submitted any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt 
of the said notice, Sh. Haidar Ali has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of 
India for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that :- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Haidar Ali, has 
failed to lodge account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act,1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Haidar Ali, R/o D.S. Andh Mahavidhyalaya, P.K. Road, New 
Delhi, GPO Central, Delhi-110001 and a contesting candidate from 40-New Delhi Assembly Constituency in General 
Election to the Legislative Assembly of National Capital Territory of Delhi, 2025, to be disqualified for being chosen 
as and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of 
a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

New Delhi, the 11th March, 2026 
O.N. 51—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of National Capital Territory of 


Delhi, 2025 for 40-New Delhi Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India 
Notification No. 464/ECI/DL-LA/2025, dated 10"J anuary, 2025; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent 
under Section 77 of the said act; and

WHEREAS, the result of the election for 40-New Delhi Assembly Constituency of National Capital Territory 
of Delhi, 2025 was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" February, 2025 and hence the last date for lodging the 
account of Election Expenses was 10" March, 2025; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 11.03.2025 of DEO, New Delhi under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi vide his letter No. 
CEO/COE/102(121)/2024/1637 dated 26.03.2025, Sh. Virender, a contesting candidate from 40-New Delhi 
Assembly Constituency of National Capital Territory of Delhi, 2025 has failed to lodge account of election expenses, 
as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ 
No. 76/दिल्ली वि0स0/व्यय लेखा/2025/सी0ई0एम0एस0-1, dated 297 April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 
89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Virender, for not lodging of 


account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Virender, was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission explaining 
the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of election expenses with the District Election 
Officer, New Delhi, District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi, has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to 
Sh. Virender, on dated 07.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, New Delhi in his Supplementary Report dated 16.07.2025 has 
reported that Sh. Virender, has not submitted any statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of 
the said notice, Sh. Virender has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India 
for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that :- 
“Tf the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Virender, has 
failed to lodge account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act,1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Virender, R/o A-302, Ground Floor, A-Block, Khanpur, JJ 
Colony, Dr. Ambedkar Nagar, New Delhi-110062 and a contesting candidate from 40-New Delhi Assembly 
Constituency in General Election to the Legislative Assembly of National Capital Territory of Delhi, 2025, to be 
disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly 
or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.
